headline: High risk of filesystem/git conflict and medium prompt-injection/cascade exposure when Gemini CLI is paired with plano; compliance risk is low due to limited shared data classes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read repo files, use MCP, and process stdin/stdout; plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and config files. If Gemini forwards untrusted file or MCP content into plano, prompt injection can cross the pair. The shared channel is plausible but not proven by docs, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI passes file or MCP content into plano prompts without sanitization
IF plano returns instructions that Gemini CLI treats as authoritative
mitigations: Disable MCP sources that ingest untrusted content
Add a fixed system prompt that ignores instructions from files and logs
Manually inspect any plano-generated text before reuse
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, while plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and agentic signals. If either agent forwards those contents through its broad network egress, sensitive workspace data can leak across the pair. The profiles show a plausible shared-data path, but not a guaranteed one.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI sends repo files or shell environment data to external APIs
IF plano exports logs, traces, or metrics containing user content to a remote service
mitigations: Redact secrets before either agent runs
Restrict both agents to a local test workspace
Turn off verbose logging in plano
Review outbound requests for file contents
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state; its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. plano exposes config files and is not documented as providing locking or coordination. That makes simultaneous writes to shared mutable state a realistic default conflict, with possible irreversible repo corruption.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or config directory
IF either agent writes while the other is reading or editing the same files
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Serialize edits with a human gate
Commit or stash before switching agents
Use read-only mode for one agent
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code or file edits, and plano can consume API/chat outputs. If plano treats Gemini's output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream routing or configuration decisions. The pair lacks documented verification or provenance controls, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF plano uses Gemini-generated text as input to routing or configuration decisions
IF no human or automated verification step checks Gemini output before plano acts on it
mitigations: Require a review step before plano consumes Gemini output
Ask Gemini to cite file paths and commands explicitly
Compare outputs against source files manually
Limit plano to advisory mode
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoff

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source tools, and the touched data classes are mostly code, files, logs, and traces rather than regulated personal data. I do not see a documented residency or certification mismatch between them, so compliance risk is limited and mainly arises only if the operator routes regulated data through either agent.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into the shared workspace or logs
IF either agent is used in a jurisdiction-specific workflow without a separate policy review
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Disable or minimize logging
Use a non-production dataset
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA boundaries
